groups.statement: Experimentally compare AI x-risk arguments, framings and outreach formats for persuasive efficacy across different audiences.
Run a randomized or quasi-random, adequately powered study with standard metrics measuring counterfactual career impact of AI safety talent programmes.
Replicate METR's AI coding RCT with more, experienced developers and varied setups to test whether AI tools slow experienced developers.
Measure how much AI safety research outputs contribute to capabilities versus safety, e.g. via citations or output classification.
Measure whether separated LLM encoder and decoder instances can coordinate on a steganographic scheme without prior communication.
Test whether diverse learners and architectures converge on the same, human-like abstractions of real-world environments.
Survey researchers to test whether pessimism about AI risk correlates with pessimism or risk attitudes in other domains.
Rerun reward-hacking generalization experiments using RL methods (PPO, DPO, expert iteration, on-policy RL) instead of supervised fine-tuning.
Evaluate whether untrusted monitor models can coordinate on Schelling points to collude, across conditions like temperature, blacklist size, and prompts.
Test generalizability, long-term behavioral effects and unintended side effects of self-other overlap fine-tuning for reducing LLM deception.
Replicate reward-hacking generalization results across more models, architectures, scales and frontier models.
Test whether adversarial-training robustness of genomic foundation models against one attack family transfers to other biologically plausible attack methods.
Measure, via controlled studies or firm data on real tasks, whether current AI tools increase workers' quality-adjusted productivity.
Compare growth of generative-AI-era startups against earlier cohorts, using prestigious-VC-funded samples or later YC 1-year outcomes.
Detect and measure unverbalized evaluation awareness using probes, activation oracles or autoencoders, separately from verbalized awareness.
Measure how well human auditors, possibly AI-aided and given varying research time, detect problems in unfamiliar AI-generated code.
Construct a toy model that demonstrates gradient hacking of SGD in practice, including models lacking reflective access to their internals.
Train game-playing agents purely via self-play without human/expert data and compare performance and strategies to human-initialized versions.
Survey AI safety and governance organisations on how many hires they plan per role, to assess talent constraints.
Ask multiple differently framed questions on AI risk in surveys and test whether responses converge or show framing effects.
Rerun earlier expert surveys on AGI timelines and AI risk to measure shifts since GPT-4 and ChatGPT.
Apply trained paraphrasers to steganographic LLM outputs and measure whether hidden information is destroyed while answer quality is preserved.
Count the people working directly on AI safety and existential risk reduction, updating earlier headcount estimates.
Train networks against interpretability methods and test whether they learn uninterpretable representations, including via circuitous routes.
Demonstrate whether AI models can collude with each other to evade untrusted monitoring, including via honeypot audits.
Test whether a model can manipulate its own activations to evade or disrupt probes trained on its internals.
Prove whether time-complexity-biased (speed prior, minimal circuit) training can produce deceptive models, as simplicity bias can.
Survey frontier AI researchers or collect systematic data to estimate how much AI accelerates AI R&D.
Analyse LLM activation trajectories across successive tokens, e.g. with PCA phase portraits, to find attractors or laws of motion.
Compare how human and AI agent success rates scale with task length or time budget on METR-style tasks.
Compare SAE feature directions across layers or model pairs to test whether they are universal, possibly up to rotation.
Ask a newly released model questions about dated events to infer its training-data knowledge cutoff.
Test whether combining human-feedback training with task decomposition into subproblems scales to significantly harder tasks.
Test whether SGD training matches singular learning theory's predictions of Bayesian posterior preferences, such as loss-lowering, complexity-increasing transitions.
Train RL agents or toy networks and test whether shard-theory predictions about learned values and selected behaviours hold.
Test how narrative framing, content length and format of AI existential risk communication affect public awareness, across multiple countries.
Test interpretability methods (SHIFT, probes, model diffing, others) on detecting misaligned model organisms without knowing their goals.
Measure how chain-of-thought obfuscation ability scales with model size and across model families up to frontier scale.
Ask AI subfield experts what fraction of the way to human-level performance their subfield has progressed recently, extending Hanson's metric.
Measure whether radical AI pause advocacy or framing produces net safety gains through radical flank effects, versus harms to advocates.
Evaluate control protocols against attack policies that choose when to attack, and measure models' attack-selection ability.
Conduct case studies of AI capability diffusion in non-LLM domains and compare them with existing LLM pretraining case studies.
Test whether steering vectors and their effects transfer across architectures, sizes, and MoE models.
Catalog key AI insights, who discovered each, and how many resources each discovery required.
Compare actual AI progress, such as METR horizon growth, against the AI 2027 scenario's forecast timeline and quantify the gap.
Measure replication and emulation lag times for AI models other than GPT-3 and compare them with GPT-3's rates.
Measure the duration and trajectory of human-AI centaur/cyborg periods across domains like chess, Go, poker and classification.
Recompute AI timeline forecasts assuming brain compute is orders of magnitude higher than standard estimates (e.g., microtubules, per-neuron ANN costs).
Count how many candidate historical examples AI Impacts investigated that turned out not to be discontinuous progress, to estimate base rates.
Estimate the ratio between available AI safety job positions and qualified applicant talent using a rigorous methodology.
